transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Lin (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Gomez (CTO, Acero), Liam O'Connor (Head of Platform), Sadia Rahman (Security Engineer)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Acero Health's networking constraints for a Private / VPC deployment of Redwood. Topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink (interface endpoints), CIDR overlap, cross-account routing, region availability, egress requirements, KMS / key management, audit logs and SOC2 controls. Next steps and owners at end.

Transcript:
00:00 Jamie: hey everyone thanks for joining, um i'm jamie from redwood inference, i'll do a super quick intro then pass to raj for the deep net questions, sound good?
00:10 Maya: yep thanks jamie, appreciate it. quick context - we're building clinical decision support workflows and we need private deployment; data residency and PHI rules, so VPC-only is a requirement.
00:20 Liam: also timing is tight, pilot in 6 weeks if we can clear security.
00:28 Raj: great, thanks. quick q - which cloud and region are you planning to run in? any multi-region needs?
00:34 Maya: primary is AWS us-east-2 (Ohio), possibly us-east-1 for DR, we prefer not to cross regions if avoidable.
00:43 Raj: ok, noted. Redwood Private can be deployed into your VPC via VPC peering or interface endpoints (PrivateLink). Both have tradeoffs - peering is lower latency but not transitive, PrivateLink is more controlled and supports cross-account interface endpoints.
01:02 Sadia: are there limits on IP ranges? we run out of /16's in some prod accounts, CIDR overlap has bitten us before.
01:08 Raj: yeah you can run into overlap. For peering you need non-overlapping CIDR blocks. For PrivateLink you put an interface endpoint in your subnet so overlap is less of a hard blocker but you still need available ENI IPs.
01:22 Liam: if we use Transit Gateway will that help with transitive routing? we do have a hub VPC model.
01:28 Raj: Transit Gateway can solve transitive routing but note Redwood doesn't depend on your TGW; we'd peer or provide endpoints into the account. If you want us behind a TGW you can route there, but you need to ensure route table propagation and no conflicting route priorities.
01:40 Maya: can you clarify NAT / egress? some of our controls force all egress through a proxy.
01:46 Jamie: yes, Redwood can be configured to use egress via your NAT/proxy. For hosted telemetry calls we can also provide private S3 endpoints for model artifact access so traffic doesn't leave the VPC.
01:58 Sadia: KMS - keys must be customer-managed, HSM backed where possible. Can you integrate with our KMS?
02:05 Raj: we support customer KMS for secrets and keys; for Private deployments you can bring your key material via AWS KMS or a supported HSM. We'll need an IAM role or cross-account access for the key usage.
02:18 Liam: what about certs for private endpoints? we use internal PKI.
02:23 Raj: interface endpoints use AWS certificate handling; we can bring a cert at the application layer if you have a private CA. There's sometimes mapping required for SANs - we'll put that in the network diagram.
02:36 Maya: compliance - SOC 2, audit logs - do you ship logs to our account?
02:41 Jamie: for Private we can stream audit logs to your logging account (CloudWatch / S3) and we can forward access logs. That's in the security whitepaper i'll share.
02:51 Sadia: any hard dependencies on specific AZs?
02:55 Raj: No, we recommend spreading across AZs; but we ask for subnets in at least two AZs. If your region only has two AZs that's fine.
03:05 Liam: region availability - any regions you don't support?
03:09 Raj: We support most commercial AWS regions; a few newer regions require extra provisioning lead time. us-east-2 is supported. If you need govcloud or specialized regions we have an enterprise path.
03:20 Maya: ok, sounds good. how do you handle model updates? we can't have sudden regressions during pilot.
03:26 Jamie: we have version pinning and rollout controls - canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous model if errors spike. Redwood Console exposes the rollouts and evals.
03:36 Sadia: can we host models inside the VPC so weights never leave our network?
03:41 Raj: yes in Private we can keep model artifacts in your account (S3 private endpoints) and runtime runs in your VPC. For Dedicated vs Private - Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood-run infra; Private is customer-managed VPC deployment.
03:58 Liam: cost question - is Dedicated cheaper than Private?
04:03 Jamie: depends. Dedicated is our managed GPUs for predictable throughput; Private has more customer ops but avoids egress costs and can leverage your committed discounts. We'll send a cost comparison.
04:16 Maya: security review will want a network diagram and list of required peering connections, ports, and ports used.
04:22 Raj: yes we'll provide a sample diagram. Key ports: 443 for control plane endpoints, and a few high-range ephemeral ports for runtime. We'll enumerate exact port/protocols in the doc.
04:35 Sadia: internal note - do you support SAML/SSO for console?
04:38 Jamie: yes, SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning and RBAC.
04:42 Liam: what about data retention and logs? we need 7 years of audit for certain flows.
04:47 Jamie: we can export logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies. Retention is configurable on your side once sent.
04:55 Maya: latency expectations - our workflows are interactive, sub-200ms preferred for short prompts.
04:59 Raj: sub-200ms at token level is challenging for larger models; for short prompts we can often land 100-200ms depending on model/quantization and instance choice. We'll recommend model + quant profile for your latency target.
05:15 Liam: are there any known gotchas with cross-account peering and security policies?
05:19 Raj: yes, Security groups don't cross the peering boundary so you need to open SGs in each account; also route tables must be edited in both VPCs. No transitive routing through peering.
05:30 Sadia: can we have egress lockdown so only specific S3 buckets are reachable?
05:34 Raj: yes via VPC endpoints and policies; we can help design S3 endpoint policies to restrict to specific prefixes.
05:42 Maya: earlier you mentioned model artifacts, but we also want to ensure KV cache doesn't leak - i heard the term 'K-V cash' on another call ha - explain caching.
05:51 Raj: ha yeah transcription glitch. Our KV cache is in-memory per node; for Private deployments it's inside your VPC runtime and not shared. We can also enable ephemeral cache purging on shutdown.
06:05 Jamie: ok i'm going to recap next steps after a couple more clarifying q's - sadia any legal specific asks now?
06:11 Sadia: we need a list of sub-processors and a DPA; also need guarantee on data-at-rest encryption.
06:18 Jamie: we'll include DPA and sub-processor list. Data at rest can be customer-managed KMS.
06:24 Liam: network performance - do you recommend ENI sizing or accelerated networking?
06:29 Raj: yes, for high throughput we recommend instances with enhanced networking and sufficient ENI bandwidth. We'll include recommended instance types in the tech deep dive.
06:37 Maya: one more question - routing across regions for DR, we'd rather keep copies in us-east-1 but not serve traffic there unless failover. how does Redwood handle region failover?
06:47 Raj: we can set up passive replicas in another region and promote them on failover. That's extra ops but doable; we'll document replication approach and RTO.
06:58 Jamie: ok thanks. i'm going to summarize next steps - we'll send the network diagram and security whitepaper, raj will validate peering vs privatelink recommendation and run compatibility checks, and we'll propose dates for a deeper technical session.
07:12 Maya: sounds good.

[Minor crosstalk]

End of recording
